title: DGX-Spark board.json
$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH (dtu/<CAMPAIGN>.1): this file IS the source.json — sweep-status.md, criterion-matrix.html AND sweep-explorer.html all render from it; none re-aggregates S3 independently. VIEWS/LENSES (consumer-side derivations over the same measurements[]; no extra data needed): (1) canonical/as-run — per-cell headline = the measurement flagged measurement.canonical (matches benches[].canonical_condition, else the closest deviation), marked (see $defs/score). (2) conditional / deviation/uplift — show all measurements for a cell and their delta along one chosen condition axis; the reference for an axis is condition_dims[axis].default, so delta = value - (value at default on that axis). (3) higher-of / max — max(value) over status=measured rows regardless of condition, labelled as a ceiling (NOT cross-comparable when reached under different conditions). HONESTY GATE: a cell renders as one clean number ONLY when score.headline_eligible=true; otherwise renderers MUST show paired on/off as-run + the truncation/null/loop diagnostics (truncation_rate/null_rate/loop_rate/overflow_rate) and force NO single number.
description: Data contract for the open-weight benchmark board. Produced by scripts/update-sweep-status.sh --emit-json from the result.json files. The published page (docs/board/index.html) fetches this and hydrates the table + charts. Condition-aware: each (model, bench) cell carries N measurements grouped by a condition (thinking, harness, quant, context, max_turns, wall_cap, ...), so thinking off/on, harness-mod uplift, budget sweeps, and quant comparisons are all one mechanism. CANONICAL = the benchmark authors' intended reference protocol, declared per bench (benches[].canonical_condition). A measurement equals canonical or is a DEVIATION from it (derived by comparing its condition to the bench's canonical_condition); the thinking-off bandage is a deviation, not canonical. The default table view is derived (show the canonical measurement if present, else the best-available deviation, marked) — it is never a stored display preference.

schema_version.description: Semver of this contract. Bump major on breaking shape changes.

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp the aggregator emitted this file. The page shows this as freshness.

condition_dims.description: Registry of the condition dimensions that can vary per measurement. Drives chart legends and the default-view selector. Open-ended: add a key to introduce a new dimension (e.g. quant).

scores.description: One entry per (model_id, bench_id) that has at least one measurement OR an explicit TBD/na status. Cells with no entry render blank.

footnotes.description: Footnote registry (dtu): the journey notes that document each cell's caveats, kept VERBATIM with a stable id so every renderer (sweep-status.md superscripts, criterion-matrix.html / sweep-explorer.html tooltips) anchors the same text. A score/measurement references entries here by id via footnote_ids. Migrated from the prose footnotes that used to live in update-sweep-status.sh; ids follow the 'note-<bd-id-or-slug>' convention.

values.description: Allowed values for this dimension, in display order.

default.description: Reference value for this axis in the deviation/uplift VIEW (decoupled from canonical, which is bench-level). Uplift deltas are computed against the measurement at this value, e.g. thinking=off (so uplift shows the effect of enabling thinking), harness=stock, max_turns=300.

value_labels.description: Optional pretty labels per value, e.g. {"<ISSUE>": "bd-227 patched"}.

family.description: qwen | gemma | nemotron | deepseek | anthropic | openai ...

params_active_b.description: Active params in billions (= total for dense).

quant.description: Default serving quant, e.g. fp8, nvfp4, awq-int4.

spark_group.description: DGX-Spark count to serve this model: 1 (single Spark), 2 (dual-Spark cluster). null = frontier / not Spark-served. Drives the table dividers.

frontier.description: True for reference comparators (Opus, GPT). Rendered in magenta, grouped separately.

thinking_only.description: True for open-weight models that the project does not run with enable_thinking=false (the off mode produces floor scores or is unsupported). Treated like frontier for the thinking-default cascade: unmarked campaigns default to thinking=on. Example: Qwen3-235B-Thinking.

profile.description: Short serving profile string for the row subtitle.

bd.description: bd issue id(s) for this model's sweep work (e.g. <CAMPAIGN>). Display only; empty when none.

hw.description: Hardware target (spark models, e.g. 'RTXPro6000 ×1') or serving endpoint (enterprise/frontier). Display only.

status.description: Plan/coverage status for the scope table, e.g. 'Pool A+B done', 'API sweep done', 'candidate — not yet run'.

tags.description: Display chips, e.g. DENSE, MOE, FRONTIER.

n.description: Task count; null when TBD (e.g. CVE-Bench before driver lands).

pool.description: A = agentic security, B = single-pass quality.

family.description: code (Pool B) | vr (vulnerability research, Pool A).

metric.description: Human label for the metric, e.g. pass@1, prompt-strict.

canonical_condition.description: The benchmark authors' intended reference protocol for THIS bench (e.g. thinking unconstrained, max_turns=300). Pin only the dims the authors specify; unpinned dims are unconstrained. A measurement whose condition matches this on all pinned dims is canonical (a headline, cross-comparable number); any difference makes it a deviation on those axes, which the page marks (ᵗ for thinking, and analogous markers for max_turns/context/etc.). Omit if the bench specifies no particular protocol (then all measurements are treated as uncontested).

value_kind.description: ratio (0..1, render bar); tier (render label like T1); count (integer).

description.description: Tooltip body for the info dot.

score.description: One (model, bench) cell. No stored display preference: the collapsed view is DERIVED — show the canonical measurement (the one matching benches[].canonical_condition on every pinned dim) if measured; otherwise show the measurement CLOSEST to canonical, where closeness is ranked by: (1) fewest deviating axes vs canonical_condition, then (2) highest n, then (3) latest completed_at. Only status=measured rows are eligible for the headline (smoke/tbd/na excluded). The shown cell is rendered with a marker per deviating axis (ᵗ for thinking, analogous for max_turns/context/etc.).

measurements.description: All measured conditions for this cell. Empty array = cell exists but nothing measured yet (render TBD). Multiple entries = comparison available (drives stacked/grouped bars).

headline_eligible.description: <CAMPAIGN>.1 honesty gate: TRUE iff this cell may render as ONE clean headline number. Computed by the aggregator, not a display preference. TRUE requires BOTH: (1) ROBUST — the reported (canonical-or-closest measured) measurement has truncation_rate AND null_rate < ~0.02 (no artifact masquerading as a result); AND (2) UNAMBIGUOUS MODE — single-mode-by-design at a defined canonical condition (e.g. frontier API at author defaults), OR both thinking modes measured with the reported mode clean. FALSE => renderers MUST show the cell TRANSPARENTLY: paired on/off as-run values + truncation/loop diagnostic, with NO forced single number. Eligible by construction: frontier-API Pool B. Ineligible by construction: open-weight thinking-on Pool B under a fixed token budget (26B/31B), Pool A loop/analysis-paralysis cells.

headline_reason.description: Short machine slug explaining the headline_eligible verdict, e.g. frontier-single-mode | paired-clean | single-mode-clean | thinking-on-truncation | pool-a-loop | no-measured. Drives the cell's footnote/tooltip and the gate audit.

footnote_ids.description: Stable ids into the top-level footnotes[] registry that apply to this whole cell (dtu). Rendered as superscripts (md) / hover tooltips (html).

text.description: VERBATIM footnote body (markdown). Preserved across regenerations; renderers must not paraphrase.

kind.description: marker = global legend note (e.g. smoke); cell = per-(model,bench) context note. Optional.

condition.description: A point in condition-space: dim -> value. Keys must be declared in condition_dims. A measurement need only pin the dims that matter for it (others assumed at their dim default) — including pinning NOTHING when the bench's canonical_condition is omitted and the run is uncontested under all dim defaults. The canonical-view selector resolves any unpinned dim to condition_dims[dim].default at compare time, so empty objects are valid and semantically meaningful (= the measurement is the dim-defaults baseline).

value.description: Score. For value_kind=ratio, 0..1. For value_kind=tier (ExploitBench) it is avg_flags_16 = the MEAN NUMBER of lit capability flags per task (range 0..16, NOT divided by 16), the paper-native headline; it equals capability.avg_flags_16 and the ≥Tn distribution behind it lives in `capability`. For value_kind=count, an integer. null with status=tbd/na for non-numeric cells.

label.description: Optional display override for non-ratio cells, e.g. a collapsed tier-ladder hint like '≥T4 14/41' for an ExploitBench cell.

status.description: measured = real cell; smoke = smaller-N validation (marker), not canonical; tbd = scheduled; na = not applicable for this model/bench.

target.description: Runner target that produced this measurement (e.g. vllm, opus47, opus47-direct, gpt55). Provenance (<CAMPAIGN>).

canonical.description: Aggregator-computed: TRUE for the one measurement selected as this cell's canonical/reported headline (matches the bench canonical_condition, else closest-to-canonical per the score ranking). Exactly one measured row per cell is canonical when any exists. A convenience flag so every renderer agrees on the headline without re-deriving selection; the derivation itself is still documented on $defs/score.

superseded.description: Aggregator-computed: TRUE for a measurement that an equal-or-better run on the SAME condition has replaced (e.g. <CAMPAIGN> retry 0.135 superseded by 62l 0.304; a 0/11 ContextWindowExceeded artifact superseded by a clean rerun). Surfaced per-cell so the journey stays visible (dtu) instead of being silently dropped.

truncation_rate.description: <CAMPAIGN>.1.1: fraction of this measurement's generations that hit the token budget without yielding a usable answer (finish=length / near-empty parsed content). For lm-eval benches computed from the per-sample log (near-empty filtered_resps rate); for BCB equals extra.bcb_none_filter.null_rate. null = not computed (e.g. condition where it was never plumbed). A reported-mode value above the gate threshold (~0.02) forces headline_eligible=false. This is the diagnostic that makes a single number a LOWER bound, not a clean result.

null_rate.description: jdj: explicit null/None-content rate from the grader's none-filter (BCB: extra.bcb_none_filter.null_rate = null_solutions/total). Distinct from truncation_rate for non-BCB benches; coincides for BCB. null = not captured.

loop_rate.description: <CAMPAIGN>.1.1: of the truncations, the fraction classified as DEGENERATE thinking-loops (repetition/n-gram/compression heuristic on the raw <think>) — a genuine capability/robustness failure that more budget does NOT fix. null = not classifiable. RETROACTIVELY UNAVAILABLE for the 26B/31B 2lh cells (the gemma4 parser already discarded the raw think); only future runs that capture pre-parser completions can populate it.

overflow_rate.description: <CAMPAIGN>.1.1: of the truncations, the fraction classified as productive budget-OVERFLOW (reasoning ran out of room) — a recoverable artifact (more budget helps; cf. bd <ISSUE>). null = not classifiable (see loop_rate). loop_rate + overflow_rate, when both non-null, should sum to ~1 over the truncated subset.

num_concurrent.description: <CAMPAIGN>: vllm_num_concurrent at run time (provenance / reproducibility; concurrency can perturb sampling). null when not applicable (e.g. BCB uses its own client) or not captured.

tokens_out.description: <CAMPAIGN>: total output tokens for this measurement (provenance; helps read a truncation/loop cell). null when not captured.

audit.description: Audit state, e.g. replay-verified, discrepancy, unverified.

capability.description: du8.10.1: structured capability sub-score for value_kind=tier benches (ExploitBench). Carries the cumulative ≥Tn tier ladder + the 16-flag bitmap counts so the board can render a tier-ladder sparkline (collapsed) and a flag heatmap (drilldown) WITHOUT re-deriving from S3. The scalar `value` above still carries avg_flags_16 (the paper-native headline); this object carries the distribution behind it. Omit for non-tier benches.

footnote_ids.description: Stable ids into the top-level footnotes[] registry that apply specifically to THIS measurement/condition (dtu). Cell-wide notes live on the score instead.

notes.description: Per-cell footnote (free text). Prefer footnote_ids into the registry for anything that must stay verbatim/stable.

capabilityScore.description: du8.10.1: structured ExploitBench capability sub-score. Paper tier direction is CANONICAL: T1=hardest (pc_control/ace) .. T5=easiest (coverage); flag bins {0,1}=T5 {2,3,4}=T4 {5,6,7,8}=T3 {9,10,11,12,13}=T2 {14,15}=T1 (bd <ISSUE>.9). tier_reached per task = hardest (lowest-numbered) tier among lit flags. tier_ladder is CUMULATIVE (≥Tn = tasks with a tier_reached at least as hard as n, so counts are monotonically non-increasing geT5 >= geT4 >= geT3 >= geT2 >= geT1). bitmap[i] = number of tasks lighting flag i, indexed by flag_order.

n.description: Task count backing this capability score (matches measurement.n).

avg_flags_16.description: Mean NUMBER of lit flags per task across n tasks (range 0..16, NOT a fraction); equals measurement.value for tier benches. Paper-native headline metric.

tier_ladder.description: Cumulative ≥Tn counts (integers, out of n). Monotone non-increasing from geT5 (easiest) to geT1 (hardest).

bitmap.description: Per-flag lit-task counts, exactly 16 entries for ExploitBench (one per flag in flag_order). bitmap[i] = number of tasks (out of n) that lit flag i. Length is fixed at 16 so renderers can index pc_control (14)/ace (15) safely; validate-board-json.py enforces the lower bound (minItems), full JSON-Schema tooling the upper bound (maxItems).

flag_order.description: Optional flag names aligned to bitmap[] indices, T5->T1 left->right. When present must be the same length as bitmap (16). Defaults to the canonical ExploitBench 16-flag order when omitted (cov_func, cov_line, diff, asan, crash, addrof, fakeobj, caged_read, caged_write, infoleak_binary, infoleak_libc, infoleak_stack, arb_read, arb_write, pc_control, ace).

pc_control.description: Tasks lighting pc_control (flag idx 14). Broken out for quick frontier cross-reference.

ace.description: Tasks lighting ace / arbitrary code execution (flag idx 15). Broken out for quick frontier cross-reference.

salvaged_n.description: du8.10.4: number of the n tasks whose flags were SALVAGED from eb_artifacts/grade_calls.jsonl because score.json scored 0 (wall-capped / killed pre-score.json). salvaged_n > 0 means this cell is a LOWER bound — a slow model that reached a late-turn primitive after the ~5h episode wall is undercounted. Renderers surface this as the wall-cap marker (ᵂ).
